C-BROWSER-ENGINE-PROVIDER-PROCESS-202609.Summary: Deliver M1.2 as one governed change: a production CEF-backed browser engine provider running through the ordinary supervised native-plugin boundary, with engine-neutral contracts, bounded generic host prerequisites, crash-safe logical identity, headful S2 evidence, and no browser policy in the kernel. The implementation plan may decompose delivery into dependency- ordered packages, but all packages remain governed by this one spec and by one separately approved plan.
C-BROWSER-ENGINE-PROVIDER-PROCESS-202609.Problem: M1.1 proved the engine-neutral Browser Contract v1 and a real external Chromium/CDP spike, but it did not deliver a packaged CEF provider, native plugin-process integration, CEF child-process containment, host-backed browser artifacts, durable page-generation recovery, or the real headful S2 path. The current native supervisor terminates one direct child rather than an owned CEF process tree, and the native protocol has no bounded blob host call. A production provider therefore requires explicit generic extensions without creating a browser-specific kernel path or weakening stable v1 compatibility.

Goals.Goal: Run the first production CEF browser engine provider as an ordinary supervised Worldline native plugin process.
Keep CEF bindings, handles, callbacks, subprocess identities and policy out of the kernel and public browser contracts.
Preserve the eight stable Browser Contract v1.0 request and response wire forms while adding only explicitly versioned additive or experimental surfaces.
Add generic native-process-tree containment and bounded host blob access required by a multi-process provider, without browser-specific kernel mechanisms.
Make ContextId, PageId and DocumentRevision survive renderer, provider and host recovery without reviving stale ElementRefs or runtime authority.

Provide contexts/profiles, pages, navigation, observation, bounded semantic query, authorized action, capture, permission, cookie/storage primitives and download hooks needed by future M1.3 service plugins.
Prove a deterministic native-windowed/headful S2 through installation, capability discovery, native IPC, CEF, recovery and clean shutdown.
Integrate the provider with existing health, quarantine, staged upgrade, persistence, event and CI models.

Constraints.Constraint: BROWSER PROVIDER IS A NORMAL NATIVE PLUGIN PROVIDER; NO BROWSER-SPECIFIC KERNEL OR IPC BYPASS IS ALLOWED.
SPEC APPROVAL AND EXACT PLAN APPROVAL REMAIN SEPARATE; AN APPROVED PLAN IS IMMUTABLE.
CEF TYPES, POINTERS, ENUMS, CALLBACK OBJECTS, PROCESS IDS AND WINDOW HANDLES NEVER CROSS A PUBLIC WORLDLINE CONTRACT OR BECOME AUTHORITY.
CEF RENDERER, GPU, NETWORK, UTILITY, CRASHPAD AND OTHER CHILD ROLES ARE NOT WORLDLINE RUNTIMES AND RECEIVE NO WORLDLINE PRINCIPAL, TOKEN, PLUGIN IPC CHANNEL OR REUSABLE HOST AUTHORITY.
COMMANDS USE CAPABILITY RPC; EVENTS ARE POST-OUTCOME OBSERVATIONS AND NEVER DETERMINE AN RPC OR CEF CALLBACK RESULT.
OBSERVE, QUERY, NAVIGATE, ACT, CAPTURE, COOKIE/STORAGE MUTATION, DOWNLOAD CONTROL AND PERMISSION MUTATION REMAIN SEPARATELY AUTHORIZABLE OPERATIONS.
THE ENGINE PROVIDER OWNS PRIMITIVES, NOT TABS, USER HISTORY, WORKSPACES, DOWNLOAD POLICY, COOKIE UI, SEARCH, ADBLOCK OR DEVTOOLS PRODUCT POLICY.
THE EXISTING M1.1 CDP SPIKE REMAINS A REGRESSION FIXTURE AND IS NOT RENAMED OR WRAPPED AS THE PRODUCTION CEF PROVIDER.
PRODUCTION CEF SANDBOXING IS ENABLED; AMBIENT CEF INSTALLATIONS, UNSAFE DEBUG PORTS, PRIVILEGED URL SCHEMES AND UNPINNED PACKAGE ASSETS FAIL CLOSED.
NON-IDEMPOTENT OR EXTERNALLY VISIBLE BROWSER OPERATIONS ARE NEVER AUTOMATICALLY RETRIED AFTER AN UNKNOWN OUTCOME.
PROTECTED M0, S0, S1 AND M1.1 TESTS ARE NOT WEAKENED, SKIPPED OR REWRITTEN TO MAKE M1.2 GREEN.
REAL CEF EVIDENCE USES DETERMINISTIC LOCAL FIXTURES AND ONE REQUIRED WINDOWS GATE; LOCAL EVIDENCE IS NOT REPORTED AS HOSTED CI EVIDENCE.
EXACT PRODUCTION BUDGETS ARE FINITE, STARTUP-VALIDATED AND TESTABLE THROUGH INJECTED SMALL LIMITS; LIMIT EXHAUSTION RETURNS AN EXPLICIT BOUNDED FAILURE.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Worldline Shell or final page-surface composition.
Tabs, bookmarks, user-facing durable history, workspace, download-manager, cookies-policy, search, adblock or DevTools service plugins.
Production OSR, wgpu composition, frame queues, glass or GPU effects.
Claiming a complete native OS sandbox on platforms where the generic native host does not provide one.
Guaranteeing rollback of an already migrated persistent Chromium profile when the pinned CEF profile format does not support it.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: A repository-owned ADR documents process topology, CEF FFI/thread boundary, contract evolution, profile ownership, revision reservation, recovery, packaging, security defaults, licensing, upgrade limits, headful policy and OSR deferral before dependent implementation tasks execute.
The provider package is installed, activated, supervised, discovered, invoked, deactivated, restarted, quarantined and upgraded through existing generic Worldline plugin/runtime contracts.

The provider executable dispatches every CEF child role before Worldline bootstrap, and no CEF child can publish capabilities, issue State/Blob/Event host calls, or reuse inherited Worldline IPC material.

Generic process containment is established before the provider can spawn CEF children; normal shutdown, provider hard-kill and startup failure leave no owned CEF descendants in the required Windows gate.

CEF is pinned by version, platform, architecture and checksums; package assets, locale/resources, subprocess binary, notices and runtime DLL search roots are manifest-controlled and validated fail-closed.

Production starts CEF with sandboxing enabled, no ambient remote-debugging endpoint, and no production no-sandbox escape; privileged/local schemes such as file, javascript, chrome, devtools and undeclared custom schemes are denied absent a separately versioned authorized contract.

The stable Browser Contract v1.0 request/response wire fixtures remain compatible; existing browser.engine.crashed remains supported; new events are additive; capture and engine cookie/storage/download-hook contracts are declared experimental version 0.1 and do not masquerade as v1.0.

Unknown external outcomes use the existing M0.7 correlated side-effect semantics without silently converting Incomplete into Failed or Success and without automatic retry of non-idempotent operations.
Every ContextId and PageId is a Worldline logical identity with exact resource ownership checks against trusted InvocationContext; raw CEF identifiers and payload strings never create authority.

Before any DocumentRevision or ElementRef is returned or published, the provider durably reserves a strictly greater page generation; renderer/provider/host recovery reserves another generation before readiness, so no crash window can reuse a previously visible revision.
Failpoint evidence covers CEF commit, durable generation reservation, RPC completion and event publication boundaries and proves that every pre-crash ElementRef is rejected after recovery.

Persistent profiles use installation-owned confined roots and remain isolated; logical profile IDs never become paths; incognito state is never restored and abandoned ephemeral roots are cleaned during recovery.
Navigation, reload, stop and engine back/forward operate through browser.navigate/v1; engine navigation recovery remains bounded and never becomes the M1.3 user-history source of truth.

Observe returns real URL, title, loading and revision state; query returns a real bounded semantic DOM/accessibility projection; click, input, focus and submit target exact live engine nodes and reject stale, detached or cross-page references before mutation.

Untrusted action text, node keys, URLs, origins, filenames and callback values remain data and are never interpolated into executable JavaScript, CEF source, command-line switches or filesystem authority.

The experimental browser.capture v0.1 path publishes bounded bytes through generic host blob storage and returns a provider-scoped artifact reference; possession of BlobId or artifact identity alone grants no read authority.

The generic native blob protocol bounds request and response sizes, correlates calls to the current runtime/invocation, rejects stale or foreign handles, and preserves BlobStore corruption and path-confinement semantics.

Permission decisions are set/queryable only through capability RPC; a synchronous CEF callback consults the provider decision projection and fails closed when no decision exists, without waiting for an event subscriber.
Cookie and storage observation versus mutation operations are separately grantable, validate canonical context/origin ownership, and cannot cross profile boundaries.

Downloads write only to a confined staging/artifact root; absolute, traversal, UNC/device, alternate-stream, symlink/reparse and race-based escapes are rejected; final destination policy remains outside M1.2.

Renderer failure leaves the provider RuntimeId and unaffected pages alive where CEF isolation permits; provider failure revokes the old RuntimeId and handles, restarts with fresh authority, restores logical state and emits only facts the new runtime can authoritatively observe.

Provider-process failure and restart are observed through generic host lifecycle/trajectory state; browser-specific page-restored or ready events are emitted only after durable restore, and no dead provider is treated as the authoritative emitter of its own crash.

Provider and host restart restore persistent ContextId, PageId, selected-page projection, current URL and bounded engine navigation checkpoint while persistent cookies survive and incognito data does not.

Finite limits cover contexts, pages, pending RPC, CEF dispatch queue, query nodes/depth/bytes, capture pixels/bytes, event/download mailboxes, startup and shutdown; saturation tests prove explicit QueueFull/limit failures without unbounded allocation or backlog.

Provider health exposes payload-free startup duration, active context/page counts, crash/restart counts, pending RPC, engine version and last transition; metrics contain no URL body, DOM text, form input or cookies.

Staged upgrade validates a fresh ephemeral profile before switch, never mutates the active profile during stage, mints fresh RuntimeId on switch/rollback and reports persistent-profile rollback limitations truthfully.

S2 runs from a clean host through real package install/activation, broker discovery, native IPC, CEF headful local navigation, event observation, semantic query/action, capture, renderer crash, provider hard-kill, state restore and orphan-free shutdown with no direct provider-library calls.

A required repository-owned BrowserProvider Windows CI suite fails when CEF is missing or broken, never succeeds by environment detection or continue-on-error, and preserves Source, Correctness, ArchitectureSecurity, ProvingSlice, RealChromium and All suites.

Windows x86_64 is the only real CEF platform claimed verified by M1.2 unless separately named evidence exists; Linux continues to prove engine-neutral contracts and architecture without a false real-provider claim.
ROADMAP marks M1.2 Done and GRACE adds M-BROWSER-ENGINE-PROVIDER with V-M-BROWSER-ENGINE-PROVIDER only after named fresh local and hosted evidence passes and the user explicitly confirms apply.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Fresh evidence names exact contract compatibility fixtures, generic process-tree and blob protocol tests, crash-window revision failpoints, CEF package/security checks, real headful S2, renderer/provider/host recovery, profile isolation, bounded backpressure, orphan-free shutdown and the required hosted Windows BrowserProvider run; local commands are reported only as local evidence.

Assumptions.Assumption: C-BROWSER-M1-1-AUDIT-REMEDIATION-20260831 is verified, explicitly confirmed applied and archived before this plan is approved or executed.
ADR-BROWSER-ENGINE-V1 remains the accepted engine-selection decision, while its external Chrome/CDP measurements are not treated as proof of CEF packaging, native embedding or windowed operation.
The generic installation StateRequest path remains the authoritative checkpoint path; exposing BlobStore to native providers requires the explicitly scoped protocol work authorized by this spec.
Windows x86_64 is the first real provider target; other platforms remain unverified until named real-provider evidence exists.
Exact crate names may follow repository conventions, but the logical separation between public contracts, provider state machine, private CEF adapter and executable entrypoint is mandatory.
The implementation plan will be a separately approved immutable document and may schedule multiple bounded worker packages under this single change.

ContractEvolution.StableSurface: browser.context/page/navigate/observe/query/act/download/permission v1.0 request and response wire forms remain supported.
ContractEvolution.AdditiveEventRule: Existing v1 events remain accepted; new renderer, revision, action and restore facts are additive and have explicit payload versions.
ContractEvolution.ExperimentalSurface: browser.capture, browser.engine.cookies, browser.engine.storage and browser.engine.download-hook use version 0.1 with experimental stability and explicit operation-level authority.
ContractEvolution.CompatibilityRule: No existing public Rust enum receives a required new variant unless a compatibility test proves the negotiated wire/API change; otherwise use an additive versioned DTO or generic M0.7 outcome surface.

RevisionSafetyProtocol.Step: Read the last durable generation for the logical PageId.
Reserve a strictly greater generation through installation-state CAS before exposing the document.
Bind the new engine document only to the reserved generation.
Return RPC results, publish commit/restore events and issue ElementRefs only after reservation succeeds.
If the engine effect occurred but durable reservation or correlated completion is unknowable, mark the side effect Incomplete, keep the page unready and do not retry automatically.
Every renderer, provider and host recovery reserves again before restored readiness.

OwnershipRules.Rule: The provider owns page, navigation, action, renderer and restore facts it directly observes.
The host owns generic runtime failure, restart, quarantine and authority revocation facts.
The provider never self-certifies the failure of a runtime that is already dead.
Permission callbacks consume a locally available decision projection populated by RPC and default to deny.
Browser service policy introduced in M1.3 may consume primitives but does not move policy into the CEF adapter.

C-BROWSER-ENGINE-PROVIDER-PROCESS-202609.ImplementationDecompositionRule: The separately approved plan must split work into dependency-ordered packages for architecture and compatibility, generic host prerequisites, provider core, CEF bootstrap/headful rendering, semantic actions and capture, profiles/persistence, recovery/operability, and CI/S2 closure. Each package must declare exact observed write scope, verification and stop conditions; no package may claim the whole milestone complete before final S2 evidence.
